exposure: CTG parameters (baseline fetal heart rate, variability, accelerations, decelerations)
outcome: need for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission
cohort: The study enrolled 195 term pregnant women.
finding: Abnormal cardiotocographic (CTG) patterns were significantly associated with higher rates of cesarean sections, lower Apgar scores, and increased neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions.
mod_finding: Abnormal CTG patterns were correlated with higher rates of cesarean sections, and CTG monitoring was utilized to predict the mode of delivery.
